  <title>Governor Stein, NCDMVA Encourage Employers to Hire Veterans and Military Spouses at Wilmington Roadshow</title>
  <link>https://governor.nc.gov/news/press-releases/2026/10/28/governor-stein-ncdmva-encourage-employers-hire-veterans-and-military-spouses-wilmington-roadshow</link>
  <description><span class="field field--name-title field--type-string field--label-hidden">Governor Stein, NCDMVA Encourage Employers to Hire Veterans and Military Spouses at Wilmington Roadshow</span>

  <div class="field field--name-field-release-date field--type-datetime field--label-above">
    <div class="field__label">Release Date</div>
              <div class="field__item"><time datetime="2026-10-28T12:00:00Z" class="datetime">Wed, 10/28/2026 - 12:00</time>
</div>
          </div>
<span class="field field--name-uid field--type-entity-reference field--label-hidden"><span>sengel</span></span>
<span class="field field--name-created field--type-created field--label-hidden"><time datetime="2026-10-28T15:02:43-04:00" title="Wednesday, October 28, 2026 - 15:02" class="datetime">Wed, 10/28/2026 - 15:02</time>
</span>

            <div class="clearfix text-formatted field field--name-body field--type-text-with-summary field--label-hidden field__item"><p>Today Governor Josh Stein joined the North Carolina Department of Military and Veterans Affairs at the Unlock the Veteran &amp; MilSpouse Advantage Roadshow in Wilmington to encourage employers to support veterans and military spouses.</p><p>“North Carolina servicemembers and veterans have answered the call to serve and defend us, and we owe them a deep debt of gratitude for defending our freedom and safety here and abroad,” <strong>said Governor Josh Stein.</strong> “Hiring veterans and military spouses is a win-win for employers and for military families building successful futures in our state.”</p><p>“With more than 600,000 veterans calling North Carolina home — and thousands of service members transitioning out of the military each year — they are an incredible asset to our workforce and a strength to our economy,” <strong>said North Carolina Department of Military and Veterans Affairs Secretary Jocelyn Mitnaul Mallette, a United States Air Force Veteran.</strong> “This roadshow has shown employers across the state the untapped potential of our military-connected community — their leadership, adaptability, and resilience.”</p><p>The Unlock the Veteran &amp; MilSpouse Advantage Roadshow is a statewide series connecting employers, workforce leaders, and community partners to explore how hiring from the military community strengthens North Carolina’s workforce, businesses, and economy. With more than 600,000 veterans calling North Carolina home and thousands of servicemembers transitioning each year, this initiative highlights the importance of hiring veterans and military spouses.&nbsp;</p><p>North Carolina has the fourth-largest military presence in the nation, including the most populated Army base in the world and the primary East Coast base of the Marine Corps. The state is home to more than 90,000 active-duty military personnel, more than 40,000 National Guard and Reserve servicemembers, more than 600,000 military veterans, and nearly 150,000 military family members. Governor Stein’s administration is committed to supporting North Carolina’s military families and veterans. In May, the Governor signed an executive order that directs all cabinet agencies to designate a Military Affairs Coordinator to coordinate shared efforts supporting servicemembers and recommend strategies for addressing opportunities and challenges in supporting military communities.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p><p>Last year, Governor Stein signed into law four bills that support servicemembers and their families, helping military spouses transfer their professional licenses from out of state, making it easier to remotely renew driver licenses, aiding parents enrolling their children in public schools, and helping military students afford tuition in the University of North Carolina System. In August 2025, Governor Stein announced North Carolina became a <a href="https://governor.nc.gov/news/press-releases/2025/08/06/governor-stein-underscores-commitment-supporting-military-families-joins-blue-star-families-do-your" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Do Your Part State</a> – a joint initiative between Blue Star Families and the National Governors Association that supports military families.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p><p>On November 17, Governor Stein will present six distinguished North Carolinians with the <a href="https://am.ticketmaster.com/hurricanes/buy/ncawards" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">North Carolina Award</a>, the state’s highest civilian honor, including Lt. General Kevin Vereen (Ret.), who closed his career as the Army’s Deputy Chief of Staff. Proceeds from ticket sales for the awards ceremony at the Lenovo Center in Raleigh will go to two charities that benefit veterans and military families: <a href="https://bluestarfam.org/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Blue Star Families</a> and <a href="https://www.campcorral.org/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Camp Corral</a>. Blue Star Families is a national nonprofit organization that supports military families through the challenges of military life by better connecting them with the communities they live in during their servicemembers’ military service and deployments. Camp Corral serves children of this nation’s wounded, ill, and fallen military heroes.&nbsp;</p></div>

  <title>In NC Strong Update, Governor Stein Highlights Commitments to Keep North Carolinians Safe and Lower Costs for Families</title>
  <link>https://governor.nc.gov/news/press-releases/2026/10/27/nc-strong-update-governor-stein-highlights-commitments-keep-north-carolinians-safe-and-lower-costs</link>
  <description><span class="field field--name-title field--type-string field--label-hidden">In NC Strong Update, Governor Stein Highlights Commitments to Keep North Carolinians Safe and Lower Costs for Families</span>

  <div class="field field--name-field-release-date field--type-datetime field--label-above">
    <div class="field__label">Release Date</div>
              <div class="field__item"><time datetime="2026-10-27T12:00:00Z" class="datetime">Tue, 10/27/2026 - 12:00</time>
</div>
          </div>
<span class="field field--name-uid field--type-entity-reference field--label-hidden"><span>sengel</span></span>
<span class="field field--name-created field--type-created field--label-hidden"><time datetime="2026-10-27T12:12:48-04:00" title="Tuesday, October 27, 2026 - 12:12" class="datetime">Tue, 10/27/2026 - 12:12</time>
</span>

            <div class="clearfix text-formatted field field--name-body field--type-text-with-summary field--label-hidden field__item"><p>Today Governor Josh Stein held his latest NC Strong Update to highlight ongoing initiatives to lower the cost of living for North Carolina families and keep people safe.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p><p><strong>Lowering Energy Bills</strong>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p><p>As temperatures drop and North Carolina families turn their heat on, Governor Stein continues to address the need to combat rising utility bills. The Governor’s bipartisan Energy Policy Task Force found that electricity rates could increase by as much as 70% over the next 15 years, and key factors in this increase are the large energy loads of data centers, which make up approximately 30% of new energy projects but 80% of projected future energy demand. According to a new <a href="https://governor.nc.gov/documents/files/nc-power-pathways-report/open" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">report</a> done in conjunction with the Energy Policy Task Force, data centers’ large energy loads will create $50 billion more in costs through 2050.&nbsp;</p><div class="align-center">
  
  

            <div class="field field--name-image field--type-image field--label-hidden field__item">  <img loading="lazy" src="https://files.nc.gov/nc-governor/styles/inline_large/public/images/2026-10/55614562607_00159c98b8_o.jpg?VersionId=6wxr0t8i.uZ19zje.XqNWzGgaxiZ2zEu&amp;itok=AqnGVpM1" width="959" height="640" alt class="image-style-inline-large">


</div>
      
</div>
<p>“Data centers’ large energy loads are going to create $50 billion in costs for all ratepayers, and if nothing changes, families will have to foot data centers’ bill. That’s unacceptable. We need to bring real rate relief for North Carolinians,” <strong>said Governor Josh Stein. </strong>“The Utilities Commission has the chance to protect people’s utility bills by voting to approve large load tariffs, and I am calling on the commission to get it done.”</p><p>“Families shouldn’t pay for the cost of new data centers. That’s what we’ve been fighting for in these cases," <strong>said Attorney General Jeff Jackson.</strong> "Duke’s proposal is a real step in that direction, and it puts more of the cost on the data centers, where it belongs. It’s not final yet, and we’re going to keep pushing for more.”&nbsp;</p><p>For months, Governor Stein has called for large load tariffs to protect North Carolinians from the costs of data centers’ massive energy use and urged the Utilities Commission to require data centers to pay the full cost of their impact and bring their own clean energy. Governor Stein and Attorney General Jeff Jackson <a href="https://ncdoj.gov/attorney-general-jeff-jackson-governor-stein-respond-to-duke-energys-proposal-for-ncs-first-large-load-tariff/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">recently responded</a> to Duke Energy’s proposal to create North Carolina’s first-ever large load tariff and establish rules that apply to data centers and other large energy users. Duke Energy’s settlement has important new ratepayer protections, such as requiring data centers to cover their energy grid costs. However, it falls short in other areas, such as on how to deal with generation. To fill these gaps, Governor Stein is calling for the Utilities Commission and the relevant parties to continue their work and make sure data centers pay the full cost of their impact, including generation, and bring their own clean energy.&nbsp;</p><p>Over the past year, Energy Futures worked in collaboration with the Energy Policy Task Force on energy costs and the impacts of various policies in North Carolina. Energy Futures Group’s <a href="https://governor.nc.gov/documents/files/nc-power-pathways-report/open" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">report</a> made the following findings:&nbsp;&nbsp;</p><ul><li data-list-item-id="ebad87e3ecf4e10fff01a5eb8b72e5218"><strong>Large loads will cost $50 billion over the next 25 years. </strong>In the business-as-usual scenario, large loads, a majority of which are data centers, account for 85% of new demand through 2035. The rate of load growth projected in the next 15 years is five times the rate that was seen in the past 20.&nbsp;</li><li data-list-item-id="e28f0fa18b5f1fc7f40683de9898b9855"><strong>Pursuing a net zero target reduces costs for ratepayers. </strong>If North Carolina plans for the future now, starts cutting emissions in the mid-2030s rather than later, and puts in place supportive policies like grid-enhancing technologies, it would save the ratepayers $14.6 billion compared to business as usual.&nbsp;</li><li data-list-item-id="e4ac58d0681e810a556e1c2bdad23d70c"><strong>Letting large load customers bring their own generation saves ratepayers. </strong>A program where just half of new large customers directly pay for or bring the clean energy they have committed to and operate flexibly would save other ratepayers $20 billion.&nbsp;&nbsp;</li></ul><p>Click <a href="https://governor.nc.gov/documents/files/nc-power-pathways-report/open" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">here</a> to read the report.&nbsp;</p><p><strong>Supporting Survivors of Domestic Violence</strong>&nbsp;</p><p>October is Domestic Violence Awareness Month, a time to draw attention to this heinous crime and the state's work to confront it. According to the North Carolina Coalition Against Domestic Violence, at least 66 homicides in North Carolina were direct results of domestic violence in 2025.&nbsp;</p><div class="align-center">
  
  

            <div class="field field--name-image field--type-image field--label-hidden field__item">  <img loading="lazy" src="https://files.nc.gov/nc-governor/styles/inline_large/public/images/2026-10/55615985525_3d54911e5e_o.jpg?VersionId=eRHoMAET5Pf4VlA7kTgH7ve3BDPkq_vy&amp;itok=iQPwq64n" width="960" height="640" alt class="image-style-inline-large">


</div>
      
</div>
<p>“Domestic violence is a heinous crime that is all too common. Too often, an abuser’s first victim is not their last, and several recent incidents of violence in our state were preceded by the perpetrator abusing a family member or partner,” <strong>said Governor Josh Stein.</strong> “If you are currently experiencing domestic violence or you know someone who is, resources are available to get you to safety.”&nbsp;</p><!--StartFragment--><p style="-webkit-text-stroke-width:0px;background-color:rgb(255, 255, 255);color:rgb(0, 0, 0);font-family:Roboto, sans-serif;font-size:16px;font-style:normal;font-variant-caps:normal;font-variant-ligatures:normal;font-weight:400;letter-spacing:normal;margin-bottom:0px;margin-top:16px;orphans:2;text-align:left;text-decoration-color:initial;text-decoration-style:initial;text-decoration-thickness:initial;text-indent:0px;text-transform:none;white-space:normal;widows:2;word-spacing:0px;"><span style="background-color:transparent;font-size:14px;">"At the Department of Administration, we are proud to support programs that help people leave abusive relationships through our Division for Women &amp; Youth and the NC Domestic Violence Commission," </span><strong style="background-color:transparent;font-size:14px;">said Secretary of Administration Gabe Esparza. </strong><span style="background-color:transparent;font-size:14px;">"Domestic violence does not discriminate; no matter your race, age, socioeconomic class, sexual orientation, religion or gender — abuse can happen to anyone. Each one of us can help stop the cycle of domestic violence by knowing how to spot abusive behaviors and where to direct people who need help."</span></p><p style="-webkit-text-stroke-width:0px;background-color:rgb(255, 255, 255);color:rgb(0, 0, 0);font-family:Roboto, sans-serif;font-size:16px;font-style:normal;font-variant-caps:normal;font-variant-ligatures:normal;font-weight:400;letter-spacing:normal;margin-bottom:0px;margin-top:16px;orphans:2;text-align:left;text-decoration-color:initial;text-decoration-style:initial;text-decoration-thickness:initial;text-indent:0px;text-transform:none;white-space:normal;widows:2;word-spacing:0px;"><span style="font-size:14px;">"We cannot simply tell survivors to leave. We must build the conditions that make safety possible," </span><strong style="font-size:14px;">said Representative Monika Johnson-Hostler</strong><span style="font-size:14px;">. "Survivors should not have to choose between their safety and keeping a roof over their heads or meeting their family's basic needs. We must also ensure local programs have the funding and resources to provide comprehensive services and invest in prevention."</span></p><p style="-webkit-text-stroke-width:0px;background-color:rgb(255, 255, 255);color:rgb(0, 0, 0);font-family:Roboto, sans-serif;font-size:16px;font-style:normal;font-variant-caps:normal;font-variant-ligatures:normal;font-weight:400;letter-spacing:normal;margin-bottom:0px;margin-top:16px;orphans:2;text-align:left;text-decoration-color:initial;text-decoration-style:initial;text-decoration-thickness:initial;text-indent:0px;text-transform:none;white-space:normal;widows:2;word-spacing:0px;"><span style="background-color:transparent;font-size:14px;">The NC Department of Administration’s Division for Women and Youth provides funding to 76 domestic violence programs in 97 North Carolina counties. These programs offer shelter, counseling, 24-hour crisis lines, transportation, and court and advocacy services. More than 60,000 adults and children received domestic violence services remotely and in person, and more than 100,000 crisis calls and chats were received from individuals seeking domestic violence assistance from those DOA-funded programs during fiscal year 2024-25.&nbsp;</span></p><p style="-webkit-text-stroke-width:0px;background-color:rgb(255, 255, 255);color:rgb(0, 0, 0);font-family:Roboto, sans-serif;font-size:16px;font-style:normal;font-variant-caps:normal;font-variant-ligatures:normal;font-weight:400;letter-spacing:normal;margin-bottom:0px;margin-top:16px;orphans:2;text-align:left;text-decoration-color:initial;text-decoration-style:initial;text-decoration-thickness:initial;text-indent:0px;text-transform:none;white-space:normal;widows:2;word-spacing:0px;"><span style="background-color:transparent;font-size:14px;">For additional resources, including a directory of state-funded domestic violence agencies, visit the </span><a style="color:rgb(70, 120, 134);font-size:14px;text-decoration:underline;" href="https://www.doa.nc.gov/divisions/council-women-youth" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Division for Women and Youth website</a><span style="background-color:transparent;font-size:14px;">.&nbsp;</span></p><p style="-webkit-text-stroke-width:0px;background-color:rgb(255, 255, 255);color:rgb(0, 0, 0);font-family:Roboto, sans-serif;font-size:16px;font-style:normal;font-variant-caps:normal;font-variant-ligatures:normal;font-weight:400;letter-spacing:normal;margin-bottom:0px;margin-top:16px;orphans:2;text-align:left;text-decoration-color:initial;text-decoration-style:initial;text-decoration-thickness:initial;text-indent:0px;text-transform:none;white-space:normal;widows:2;word-spacing:0px;"><strong>Strengthening 911 Services</strong>&nbsp;</p><p>Governor Stein announced that the North Carolina 911 Board has awarded more than $13 million in grant funding this year to support critical equipment upgrades and facility enhancements for public safety answering points (PSAPs) across North Carolina. These investments help ensure that the centers answering 911 calls are best equipped to serve their communities effectively and reliably.&nbsp;</p><div class="align-center">
  
  

            <div class="field field--name-image field--type-image field--label-hidden field__item">  <img loading="lazy" src="https://files.nc.gov/nc-governor/styles/inline_large/public/images/2026-10/55614562517_ac85491ed4_o.jpg?VersionId=KBo1V7GBFC_tkUfrg1xCJkw_fPbctJCl&amp;itok=ouhWk8z8" width="960" height="640" alt class="image-style-inline-large">


</div>
      
</div>
<p>“Every second matters when someone calls 911,” <strong>said Governor Josh Stein.</strong> “These grants will give 911 operators the resources and technology they need to better connect North Carolinians with the help they need quickly. And 988 is another valuable tool for people experiencing mental health crises.”</p><p>“Reliable 911 telecommunications are essential to keeping North Carolinians safe,” <strong>said NC Department of Information Technology Secretary, State Chief Information Officer, and NC 911 Board Chair Nate Denny.</strong> “Investing in the tools and capabilities our 911 centers need reinforces the trust people place in 911 and ensures every call for help is met reliably and quickly.”</p><p>“The N.C. 911 Board remains dedicated to working alongside local PSAPs, ensuring they have the resources and support needed to carry out the critical, lifesaving responsibilities that protect our communities,” <strong>said L.V. “Pokey” Harris, Executive Director of the NC 911 Board. </strong>“Year after year, the PSAP Grant Program continues to demonstrate its value as a strong, reliable source of funding that enhances the board’s annual 911 PSAP distribution and helps advance our mission.”</p><p>Over the past decade, the NC 911 Board's Grant Program has invested more than $104 million to help counties and municipalities strengthen 911 emergency communications across North Carolina. Those investments have included modernized 911 centers and radio system components, computer-aided dispatch technology, and training programs for professionals.&nbsp;</p><p><strong>This year’s grants awarded include:</strong>&nbsp;</p><p><strong>Alexander County E-911 Communications – </strong>$640,184.10 for radio console upgrades&nbsp;</p><p><strong>Bertie County Communications – </strong>$748,093.90 for radio console replacement&nbsp;</p><p><strong>Brunswick County Central Communications – </strong>$54,107.19 for cybersecurity upgrades and hardening&nbsp;</p><p><strong>Charlotte-Mecklenburg Police Communications – </strong>$1,927,216.91 for radio console replacement&nbsp;</p><p><strong>Granville County Communications – </strong>$509,202.30 for radio upgrades&nbsp;</p><p><strong>Jones/Lenoir Communications – </strong>$944,801.08 for site upgrades&nbsp;</p><p><strong>Lumberton Police Communications – </strong>$120,949.11 for backup radio upgrades&nbsp;</p><p><strong>Montgomery County 911 Communications – </strong>$615,489.02 for new primary and backup radio replacements&nbsp;</p><p><strong>NC State Highway Patrol – </strong>$4,110,916.90 for replacing radio dispatch consoles and logging recorders (<em>while not an N.C. 911 Board-funded PSAP, the Highway Patrol is eligible to receive board-funded grants pursuant to G.S. 143B-1407</em>)&nbsp;</p><p><strong>Robeson E-911 Communications – </strong>$1,090,906.72 for radio replacements&nbsp;</p><p><strong>Rutherford County Communications – </strong>$53,974.06 for radio console replacement&nbsp;</p><p><strong>Stanly County 911 – </strong>$518,913.56 for radio console replacement&nbsp;</p><p><strong>Union County Communications – </strong>$565,176.68 for radio console replacement&nbsp;</p><p><strong>Wilson County Emergency Communications – </strong>$1,255,628.73 for radio console replacement&nbsp;</p><p>The NC 911 Board, a unit of the NC Department of Information Technology, oversees the statewide effort to create and maintain an enhanced, fully integrated 911 system for all voice communication technologies.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p><p>The 911 Board manages the uniform 911 service charge collected by telephone and voice communication providers, directing this revenue into the 911 Fund. These funds support 124 public safety answering points, which are operated by counties and other local government entities throughout North Carolina and employ nearly 3,000 telecommunicators.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p><p>Anyone experiencing mental health distress can also call or text 988 or chat at <a href="https://988lifeline.org/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">988Lifeline.org</a> and speak with a trained mental health specialist. People who speak Spanish can now connect directly to Spanish-speaking crisis counselors by calling 988 and pressing option 2, texting “AYUDA” to 988, or chatting online at <a href="https://988lineadevida.org/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">988lineadevida.org</a> or <a href="https://988lifeline.org/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">988Lifeline.org</a>. For additional support, call the NCDHHS Peer Warmline at 1-855-PEERS NC (855-733-7762) to speak with a peer support specialist, someone who understands.&nbsp;</p><!--EndFragment--></div>

  <title>Governor Stein Announces Finance Services Company to Invest $11.5 Million in Charlotte Expansion</title>
  <link>https://governor.nc.gov/news/press-releases/2026/10/27/governor-stein-announces-finance-services-company-invest-115-million-charlotte-expansion</link>
  <description><span class="field field--name-title field--type-string field--label-hidden">Governor Stein Announces Finance Services Company to Invest $11.5 Million in Charlotte Expansion</span>

  <div class="field field--name-field-release-date field--type-datetime field--label-above">
    <div class="field__label">Release Date</div>
              <div class="field__item"><time datetime="2026-10-27T12:00:00Z" class="datetime">Tue, 10/27/2026 - 12:00</time>
</div>
          </div>
<span class="field field--name-uid field--type-entity-reference field--label-hidden"><span>sengel</span></span>
<span class="field field--name-created field--type-created field--label-hidden"><time datetime="2026-10-27T11:56:17-04:00" title="Tuesday, October 27, 2026 - 11:56" class="datetime">Tue, 10/27/2026 - 11:56</time>
</span>

            <div class="clearfix text-formatted field field--name-body field--type-text-with-summary field--label-hidden field__item"><p>Today Governor Josh Stein announced The Clearing House Payments Company L.L.C., a financial services provider, will add 200 jobs in Mecklenburg County. The company will invest $11.5 million to expand its operations to Charlotte.</p><p>“Charlotte is the second-largest financial center in the nation,”<strong> said Governor Josh Stein</strong>. “The Clearing House can capitalize on our state’s top-ranked business climate and top-tier talent that support the growing financial services ecosystem of our state.”</p><p>Founded in 1853, The Clearing House is one of the nation’s most experienced payments companies and banking associations, operating critical U.S. payment infrastructure that clears and settles more than $2 trillion each business day through wire, ACH, real-time payment, and check-image exchange services. Focused on systems that are secure and reliable and available to financial institutions of all sizes, The Clearing House drives payments innovation, supports industry collaboration, and provides strategic thought leadership on the future of payments. Its expansion in Charlotte will establish a modern, secure, and flexible presence that supports the company’s long-term business growth, client engagement, operational resilience, and employee experience.&nbsp;</p><p>“We’re excited to open a new office in Charlotte, one of the nation’s leading banking and financial services hubs,” <strong>said David Watson, President and Chief Executive Officer of The Clearing House.</strong> “With its deep talent pool and strong financial services community, Charlotte is an ideal location for The Clearing House to build on our longstanding presence in North Carolina and strengthen relationships with clients in the region while creating new opportunities to connect with financial institutions across the country. We look forward to becoming an even more active part of the area's thriving banking and financial services industry.”&nbsp;</p><p>“North Carolina is a national hub for the finance and fintech sectors,” <strong>said N.C. Commerce Secretary Lee Lilley.</strong> “Companies like The Clearing House can bank on the opportunities, workforce, and strategic advantages that North Carolina offers growing financial firms.”</p><p>Although wages for the positions will vary, the average annual salary will be $162,322, which exceeds the Mecklenburg County average of $90,706. These new jobs could create a potential annual payroll impact of more than $32.4 million for the region.&nbsp;</p><p>The Clearing House expansion will be facilitated, in part, by a Job Development Investment Grant (JDIG), which was approved by the state’s Economic Investment Committee earlier today. Over the course of the 12-year term of this grant, the project is estimated to grow the state’s economy by $1.3 billion. Using a formula that takes into account the new tax revenues generated by the new jobs and capital investment, the JDIG agreement authorizes the potential reimbursement to the company of up to $2,430,000, spread over 12 years. State payments occur only following performance verification each year by the departments of Commerce and Revenue that the company has met its incremental job creation and investment targets.&nbsp;</p><p>The project’s projected return on investment of public dollars is 282 percent, meaning for every dollar of potential cost to the state, the state receives $3.82 in state revenue. JDIG projects result in positive net tax revenue to the state treasury, even after taking into consideration the grant’s reimbursement payments to a given company.&nbsp;</p><p>Because The Clearing House chose a site in Mecklenburg County, classified by the <a href="https://www.commerce.nc.gov/grants-incentives/county-distress-rankings-tiers" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">state’s economic tier system</a> as Tier 3, the company’s JDIG agreement also calls for moving as much as $810,000 into the state’s Industrial Development Fund – Utility Account. The Utility Account helps rural communities anywhere in the state finance necessary infrastructure upgrades to attract future business.&nbsp;</p><p>“This announcement highlights the important role that financial services play in supporting job creation in Mecklenburg County and in the state,”<strong> said Senator Caleb Theodros. </strong>“We are excited for the new opportunities The Clearing House and its new operation will bring to communities.”</p><p>“We appreciate the investment The Clearing House is making in Charlotte,”<strong> said Representative Becky Carney</strong>. “This expansion brings new jobs, strengthens our business environment, and reinforces the positive impact the financial services sector has on our economy.”</p><p>In addition to the North Carolina Department of Commerce and the Economic Development Partnership of North Carolina, other key partners in this project include the North Carolina General Assembly, Commerce’s Division of Workforce Solutions, the North Carolina Community College System, Mecklenburg County, and the City of Charlotte.&nbsp;</p></div>

            <div class="clearfix text-formatted field field--name-body field--type-text-with-summary field--label-hidden field__item"><p>Today Governor Josh Stein announced the following Special Superior Court judge nominations:&nbsp;</p><p><strong>Caitlin Poe</strong>, to fill the vacancy created when the Honorable Julianna Earp retired.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p><ul><li data-list-item-id="ec86649d19f01a09dd92229371c8f21b4">Poe has served as a litigation attorney since 2013 and is currently a partner at Williams Mullen. She also clerked for Judge James Dever III on the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of North Carolina. She received her Bachelor of Arts from the University of Georgia and her Juris Doctor from the University of Virginia School of Law.&nbsp;</li></ul><p><strong>Richard Worf</strong>, to fill<strong> </strong>the vacancy created when the Honorable Michael Robinson retired.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p><ul><li data-list-item-id="eab76c32268dd2aff74b02016ed5ec914">Worf currently serves as a shareholder at Robinson, Bradshaw &amp; Hinson, P.A. and has represented clients in civil litigation for nearly 19 years. He received his Bachelor of Arts from Harvard University and his Juris Doctor from Yale Law School.&nbsp;&nbsp;</li></ul><p>“These two new judges are attorneys experienced in complex commercial litigation who have dedicated themselves to the practice of the law,” <strong>said Governor Josh Stein. </strong>“Their judgment and experience will be invaluable, and I look forward to their service on the bench.”</p><p>Governor Stein sent the nominations to the General Assembly, which must confirm the appointments by joint resolution.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p></div>

  <title>Governor Stein's October Column: It’s Too Expensive. Let’s Start Acting Like It All Year Round.</title>
  <link>https://governor.nc.gov/news/press-releases/2026/10/26/governor-steins-october-column-its-too-expensive-lets-start-acting-it-all-year-round</link>
  <description><span class="field field--name-title field--type-string field--label-hidden">Governor Stein's October Column: It’s Too Expensive. Let’s Start Acting Like It All Year Round.</span>

  <div class="field field--name-field-release-date field--type-datetime field--label-above">
    <div class="field__label">Release Date</div>
              <div class="field__item"><time datetime="2026-10-26T12:00:00Z" class="datetime">Mon, 10/26/2026 - 12:00</time>
</div>
          </div>
<span class="field field--name-uid field--type-entity-reference field--label-hidden"><span>sengel</span></span>
<span class="field field--name-created field--type-created field--label-hidden"><time datetime="2026-10-26T12:15:30-04:00" title="Monday, October 26, 2026 - 12:15" class="datetime">Mon, 10/26/2026 - 12:15</time>
</span>

            <div class="clearfix text-formatted field field--name-body field--type-text-with-summary field--label-hidden field__item"><p>This month Governor Josh Stein is providing updates on his work to lower the cost of living. Media outlets are invited to publish the column below from Governor Stein.&nbsp;</p><p>--&nbsp;</p><p>If you saw your gas prices drop a few weekends ago and wondered what happened, you’re not the only one. On October 8, the average price of gas in North Carolina was $4.10 a gallon; today, it’s $3.45, the lowest in the nation. That’s because on October 9, I signed into law a bill suspending the state gas tax until the end of November. It was a bipartisan bill, and I thank the General Assembly for pushing the action through.&nbsp;</p><p>I signed this law because people need relief now. North Carolina families are feeling the squeeze every time they fill up their gas tanks, buy groceries, pay their electric bills, or take care of their children. The cost of living is too high across the country.&nbsp;</p><p>But let’s be clear: We should not wait until right before an election to take action; costs are too high all year round.&nbsp;</p><p>North Carolinians struggle in January when the heating bill arrives. They struggle in the spring when child care payments come due. They struggle in the summer when they have to fill up the tank to get to work, buy groceries for their families, and keep the lights on.&nbsp;</p><p>Housing costs are too high, and North Carolina will need an estimated 750,000 additional homes over the next four years to meet demand. Health care costs are so burdensome that some people are skipping medications and putting off appointments they need. Electricity costs are rising, and the General Assembly continues to pass policies that threaten to push those bills even higher. Child care remains out of reach for too many parents, with roughly five families competing for every available child care slot. And federal tariffs are driving up grocery costs even as changes under H.R. 1 threaten food assistance for families who depend on SNAP. So, suspending the gas tax to respond to the war in Iran is one temporary step, but it cannot be the last.&nbsp;</p><p>Since my first day in office, my administration has worked to make life more affordable for North Carolinians. We have relieved more than $6.5 billion in medical debt for 2.5 million people through the largest medical debt relief program in the nation’s history. We established a bipartisan Health Care Affordability Commission to identify ways to get health care costs under control. And I signed an executive order focused on building more housing and bringing down housing costs.&nbsp;</p><p>Through our Energy Saver Program, we have helped participating families reduce their power bills by nearly $1,000 a year. And when the General Assembly passed legislation instructing Duke Energy to raise costs on everyday customers while lowering them for large corporations, I vetoed it. Unfortunately, legislators overrode that veto, leaving families facing higher costs to power their homes. Now, I am calling on the Utilities Commission to approve large load tariffs so that families do not foot data centers’ bill.&nbsp;</p><p>We are taking action because affordability is not a seasonal concern. It is a responsibility we have every day.&nbsp;</p><p>For two consecutive years, I have proposed a Working Families Tax Credit to help low- and moderate-income workers keep more of what they earn. For qualifying families, that credit could mean as much as $823 a year – money that could help cover groceries, gas, school supplies or an overdue bill. Yet legislators have refused to take it up.&nbsp;</p><p>I have also proposed a refundable Child and Dependent Care Tax Credit to help parents manage the cost of child care. Most children under age 5 have both parents in the workforce. When child care is unaffordable, parents can be forced to cut their hours, turn down employment opportunities, or leave their jobs altogether. Helping families afford care strengthens our kids’ futures, our workforce, and our economy.&nbsp;</p><p>I also proposed a sales tax holiday for back-to-school items, stronger unemployment benefits for workers who lose their jobs through no fault of their own, free community college for students pursuing high-demand skills, and free breakfast for schoolchildren so they can start the day healthy and ready to learn.&nbsp;</p><p>These are some concrete and practical ways to give families breathing room and help people build a more secure future. Yet instead of acting on these proposals, the General Assembly continues to protect tax breaks for corporations, their out-of-state shareholders, and the wealthiest North Carolinians.&nbsp;</p><p>It’s a question of priorities. And, right now, too many priorities are upside down.&nbsp;</p><p>I will work with anyone – Republican, Democrat, or unaffiliated – who is serious about making life more affordable for North Carolinians. There is no reason working families should have to wait for another election cycle to get help we can deliver today.&nbsp;</p><p>North Carolina families need more than temporary relief. They need leaders who show up, do the work, and deliver results.&nbsp;</p><p>Life’s too expensive all year round. Let’s start acting like it.&nbsp;</p></div>

  <title>Governor Stein Announces $149 Million Expansion for US Conec </title>
  <link>https://governor.nc.gov/news/press-releases/2026/10/22/governor-stein-announces-149-million-expansion-us-conec</link>
  <description><span class="field field--name-title field--type-string field--label-hidden">Governor Stein Announces $149 Million Expansion for US Conec </span>

  <div class="field field--name-field-release-date field--type-datetime field--label-above">
    <div class="field__label">Release Date</div>
              <div class="field__item"><time datetime="2026-10-22T12:00:00Z" class="datetime">Thu, 10/22/2026 - 12:00</time>
</div>
          </div>
<span class="field field--name-uid field--type-entity-reference field--label-hidden"><span>bwood</span></span>
<span class="field field--name-created field--type-created field--label-hidden"><time datetime="2026-10-22T13:07:57-04:00" title="Thursday, October 22, 2026 - 13:07" class="datetime">Thu, 10/22/2026 - 13:07</time>
</span>

            <div class="clearfix text-formatted field field--name-body field--type-text-with-summary field--label-hidden field__item"><div><p paraid="1875751686" paraeid="{a6d86f13-8218-4694-b4c2-fcc3042f4f8b}{48}">Today Governor Josh Stein announced US Conec Ltd., a global leader in the design, development, and manufacturing of high-density optical interconnects, will add 224 new jobs in Catawba County. The company will invest more than $149.7 million to build a state-of-the-art manufacturing facility in Hickory.&nbsp;</p></div><div><p paraid="1861170764" paraeid="{a6d86f13-8218-4694-b4c2-fcc3042f4f8b}{100}">“North Carolina companies appreciate the advantages of operating in our state,” <strong>said Governor Josh Stein.</strong> “US Conec’s decision to expand here validates the strength of our manufacturing base, our skilled talent, and our stable business climate.&nbsp;</p></div><div><p paraid="1773770145" paraeid="{a6d86f13-8218-4694-b4c2-fcc3042f4f8b}{146}">Headquartered in Hickory since its founding in 1992, US Conec provides industry-leading components worldwide for advanced computing infrastructure, enterprise networks, telecommunications networks, circuit board interconnects, and industrial and military markets. This expansion will add a 200,000-square-foot building for advanced manufacturing, research and development, administrative operations, and distribution.&nbsp;</p></div><div><p paraid="1258688924" paraeid="{a6d86f13-8218-4694-b4c2-fcc3042f4f8b}{188}">“The support of our state leaders for US Conec's expansion is great news for North Carolina, for Catawba County, and for our industry,” <strong>said Tracey Horton, president of US Conec. </strong>“The expansion will create highly skilled jobs, enhance US Conec's manufacturing capabilities in Catawba County and help meet growing demand driven by deployments of advanced computing infrastructure. We appreciate the attractive environment North Carolina has created for advanced manufacturing and look forward to continuing to invest in our team, our operations, and the communities where we work.”&nbsp;&nbsp;</p></div><div><p lang="EN-US" paraid="1377693907" paraeid="{7b17ce81-d9ba-47d9-9226-7993952c7cba}{188}">“This expansion is more great news for our innovation economy and the advanced computing supply chain in Catawba County,”<strong> said N.C. Commerce Secretary Lee Lilley.</strong> “Investments like these help position rural communities to compete for high-demand industries as it attracts global companies that will create more jobs and increase resiliency."&nbsp;</p></div><div><p paraid="1063063578" paraeid="{a6d86f13-8218-4694-b4c2-fcc3042f4f8b}{254}">While wages for engineers, operators, technicians, and support staff vary, the annual average salary for the new positions will be $56,982, which exceeds the Catawba County average of $56,937. These new jobs could potentially create an annual payroll impact of more than $12.7 million for the region.&nbsp;</p></div><div><p paraid="293501104" paraeid="{3c81e962-41e8-422b-9f82-e50b8d7eaf07}{55}">A performance-based grant of $500,000 from the One North Carolina Fund will help the company expand in North Carolina. The OneNC Fund provides financial assistance to local governments to help attract economic investment and to create jobs. Companies receive no money upfront and must meet job creation and capital investment targets to qualify for payment. All OneNC grants require matching participation from local governments, and any award is contingent upon that condition being met.&nbsp;</p></div><div><p paraid="1861045831" paraeid="{3c81e962-41e8-422b-9f82-e50b8d7eaf07}{101}">“This is another great win for Catawba County and the entire State of North Carolina,” <strong>said Senator Mark Hollo.</strong> “US Conec has been a great corporate citizen and we stand ready to support the company in this next phase of growth.”&nbsp;&nbsp;</p></div><div><p paraid="297875726" paraeid="{3c81e962-41e8-422b-9f82-e50b8d7eaf07}{133}">“We welcome these new jobs and investment to Hickory,” <strong>said Representative Jay Adams</strong>. “We appreciate the diligent work of the state and local officials as well as the economic development professionals that helped the company make this decision.”&nbsp;</p></div><div><p paraid="34457776" paraeid="{3c81e962-41e8-422b-9f82-e50b8d7eaf07}{159}">In addition to the North Carolina Department of Commerce and the Economic Development Partnership of North Carolina, other key partners in this project include the North Carolina General Assembly, Commerce’s Division of Workforce Solutions, the North Carolina Community College System, Catawba Valley Community College, Duke Energy, Piedmont Natural Gas, Catawba County, the City of Hickory, and the Catawba County Economic Development Corporation.&nbsp;</p></div></div>
